For a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ where $n$ is the number of trials, and $p$ is the probability of success on each trial, we have the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x}
$$

Here, we have $X∼B(3,\frac{3}{4}),$ so $X$ has the probability mass function

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{x}){(\frac{3}{4})}^{x}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{3-x}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<2) & =P(X\in {0,1}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{0}){(\frac{3}{4})}^{0}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{3-0}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{3}{1}){(\frac{3}{4})}^{1}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{3-1} \\  & =1{(\frac{3}{4})}^{0}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{3}+3{(\frac{3}{4})}^{1}{(\frac{1}{4})}^{2} \\  & ≈0.156\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
